title: 第25章 为了营地第26章 结算时刻
slug: 迷雾求生从流民开始的领主之路
content_zh:
“卡尔队长？！”
老汉斯愣了两秒，随即那张凹陷的脸上爆发出劫后余生般的狂喜。
他撑着地猛地站起来，膝盖都软了一下，却顾不上站稳，踉跄着迎上去。
“太好了，额……不，我是说——”他语无伦次地搓着手，眼眶泛红，“太巧了！卡尔大人，您也在这里！”
巴顿也站了起来，那个瘦弱的少年跟在父亲身后，怯生生却又带着崇敬地看着卡尔，小声叫了一句：
“卡尔大叔……”
卡尔随手丢下肩上的原木，几步跨到两人面前。
他那双总是带着煞气的眼睛，此刻也难得地露出几分惊喜。
“汉斯，你们怎么来了……那帮该死的达伦特杂碎，没把你们怎么样吧？”
“没、没……”
老汉斯激动得语无伦次，眼泪在眼眶里打转，
“命大，逃出来了……”
亚修坐在一旁，目光在几人身上流转。
没想到在这见鬼的迷雾里，还能遇到这种老乡见老乡的戏码。
“你们认识？”亚修插了一句。
“当然。”
卡尔转过头，脸上带着一种见到亲人般的红光，
“黑岩镇就那么大，老汉斯是矿上的老实人，以前给守备队送过炭。他那婆娘做的黑麦饼味道不错，可惜……”
说到这，卡尔眼神黯了黯，没再继续。
这时，迷雾南侧传来轻盈的脚步声。

伯尼也回来了。
他背着一大捆树枝，看到篝火旁突然多出的两张生面孔，以及正和他们热络攀谈的卡尔，碧绿的眼珠微微转了转，脸上的笑容变得有些耐人寻味。
“看来今晚很是热闹啊。”
伯尼放下东西，拍了拍手上的灰，自然地在火堆另一侧坐下。
简单的介绍后，六人围坐在篝火旁。
气氛因为这层“同乡”的关系，比往日那种死气沉沉要活跃了不少。
“说说吧。”
亚修往火里添了根柴，看着还在狼吞虎咽啃着第二块雾薯的巴顿，
“黑岩镇现在什么情况？你们是怎么进来的？”
提到这个，老汉斯咀嚼的动作停滞了。
他咽下嘴里的食物，浑身不由自主地颤抖了一下，像是回想起了什么极度恐怖的画面。
“没了……全没了。”
老汉斯放下手里的半块雾薯，双手抱着脑袋，声音嘶哑，
“那天夜里，那些达伦特人突然冲进了镇子。到处都是火，到处都是惨叫声……”
他抬起头，眼神里满是惊恐，
“我们不敢回头，更不敢停。”
“后来起了大雾，我们就这么深一脚浅一脚地走……大概走了两天两夜，实在走不动了，然后就看到了这边的火光。”
“两天？”
一直沉默听着的卡尔，手里的动作猛地一顿。
“你是说……从镇子出事那天算起，你们只在雾里走了两天？”

卡尔的声音变得有些幽深，听不出情绪。
“是、是啊。”
content_en:
"Captain Carl?!"
Old Hans was stunned for two seconds, and then his sunken face burst into ecstasy like the aftermath of a disaster.
He stood up suddenly, his knees weak, but he didn't care about standing still and staggered forward.
"Great, uh... no, I mean-" He rubbed his hands incoherently, his eyes red, "What a coincidence! Master Karl, you are here too!"
Barton also stood up. The thin young man followed his father, looked at Karl timidly but with reverence, and whispered:
"Uncle Carl..."
Karl casually dropped the log on his shoulder and stepped in front of the two of them.
His eyes, which were always filled with evil spirits, rarely showed a bit of surprise at this moment.
"Hans, why are you here... Those damn Darent bastards didn't do anything to you, did they?"
"No, no..."
The old Hans was so excited that he could not speak coherently, with tears welling up in his eyes.
"I'm lucky, I escaped..."
Ash sat aside, his eyes moving on several people.
I didn't expect that in this damn fog, I could encounter this kind of drama of fellow villagers meeting fellow villagers.
"Do you know each other?" Ya Xiu interjected.
"Of course."
Karl turned his head, his face glowing as if seeing a relative,
"Black Rock Town is only that big. Old Hans is an honest man in the mine. He used to deliver charcoal to the garrison. The rye cakes made by his mother-in-law are delicious, but it's a pity..."
At this point, Karl's eyes dimmed and he didn't continue.
At this time, light footsteps came from the south side of the mist.
Bernie is back too.
He was carrying a large bundle of branches, and when he saw two new faces suddenly appeared beside the campfire, and Karl who was chatting enthusiastically with them, his green eyes rolled slightly, and the smile on his face became a little intriguing.
"It looks like it's going to be very lively tonight."
Bernie put down his things, patted the ashes on his hands, and sat down naturally on the other side of the fire.
After a brief introduction, the six people sat around the campfire.
Because of this "fellow countryman" relationship, the atmosphere was much more lively than the previous lifeless atmosphere.
"Tell me about it."
Ash added a piece of firewood to the fire and looked at Barton who was still devouring the second piece of fog potato.
"What's going on in Black Rock Town now? How did you get in?"
At the mention of this, Old Hans' chewing movements stopped.
He swallowed the food in his mouth and trembled involuntarily, as if recalling some extremely terrifying scene.
"It's gone...it's all gone."
Old Hans put down half of the fog potato in his hand, held his head in his hands, and said in a hoarse voice,
"That night, those Darent people suddenly rushed into the town. There was fire everywhere, and there were screams everywhere..."
He raised his head, his eyes full of fear,
"We dare not look back, let alone stop."
"Then there was a heavy fog, so we walked deep and shallow...for about two days and two nights, we couldn't walk anymore, and then we saw the light of fire here."
"Two days?"
Karl, who had been listening silently, suddenly stopped moving in his hands.
"You mean...from the day of the accident in the town, you only walked in the fog for two days?"
Karl's voice became a little deep, and there was no emotion.
"Y-yeah."
